title: EU AI Act for fintech: what August 2026 actually requires
linkedinPost:
The EU AI Act just gave fintech operators 16 more months. Most will waste them.

The Digital Omnibus deferred high-risk AI compliance from August 2026 to December 2027 for Annex III systems — credit scoring, AML, fraud detection (Gibson Dunn, January 2026).

That covers the majority of production AI at regulated financial institutions.

But the compliance build timeline did not change. A financial institution with 5–10 high-risk systems takes 12–18 months from inventory to conformity. December 2027 does not feel far when you start counting from mid-2026.

And 2 obligations were not deferred at all:

• AI literacy (Article 4) — required since February 2025. If you haven't run a documented literacy programme, you're already out of compliance.
• Prohibited practices (Article 5) — active since February 2025. AML and fraud scoring systems need to be reviewed against this list now.

What I would actually do with the 16 months:

• Run the AI inventory this quarter — enumerate every system before classifying risk
• Wire Article 12 logging into your DORA incident infrastructure — both require it, build once
• Start AI literacy immediately — it's the cheapest obligation and the first auditors check
• Design human oversight (Article 14) as a product feature, not a compliance bolt-on

Revenue per employee rises when compliance infrastructure runs automatically — so your analysts are diagnosing decisions, not reconstructing them from memory.

Full piece + the 4-Phase Compliance Build I use to structure this — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What AI systems in fintech are classified as high-risk under the EU AI Act?

acceptedAnswer.text: Credit scoring, loan approval, AML risk profiling, fraud detection, insurance underwriting, and biometric identification are all explicitly listed under Annex III. The EBA's November 2025 report found that the majority of AI use cases at supervised institutions fall into this category — not a minority of edge systems.

mainEntity.name: What did the Digital Omnibus change about the August 2026 deadline?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Omnibus deferred high-risk obligations for stand-alone Annex III systems from August 2, 2026 to December 2, 2027. For AI embedded in regulated Annex I products, the deadline moves to August 2, 2028. AI literacy (Article 4) and prohibited practice rules (Article 5) were not deferred — both applied from February 2, 2025.

mainEntity.name: What are the fines for EU AI Act non-compliance in financial services?

acceptedAnswer.text: Non-compliance with high-risk AI obligations (Articles 9–14) carries fines of up to €15 million or 3% of total annual global turnover, whichever is higher (EU AI Act, Article 99). Prohibited practice violations under Article 5 carry a ceiling of €35 million or 7% of global turnover (EU AI Act, Article 99). Both thresholds apply per violation, not per firm.

mainEntity.name: How does EU AI Act compliance intersect with DORA for fintech?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both require incident logging, operational resilience frameworks, and third-party ICT risk management. AI Act Article 12 record-keeping and DORA incident reporting demand overlapping infrastructure — timestamped, queryable decision logs. Building one logging layer that satisfies both frameworks' output schemas is the correct design. Building separately creates duplicated cost and audit risk.
